text:
marta: quick heads-up: CI DAST run against staging started failing this morning after the weekend IAM housekeeping. Tests are timing out when the runner tries to mint ephemeral test creds. tagging @kevin and @sre-oncall. logs below, keeping it short.

kevin: looking. initial hypothesis: the CI runner uses a service account to call the token-issuer service which signs short-lived creds. the SA lost iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator in the tidy. that would explain token mint failures.

sre-oncall: can you paste the GH action snippet and error?

marta: here's the failing step stderr from the job: 
```
2026-05-02T09:04:11Z token-issuer: request for signed-cred failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = permission denied
2026-05-02T09:04:12Z dast-runner: starting scan against https://staging-app.internal: connect ETIMEDOUT
2026-05-02T09:04:12Z dast-runner: credential fetch failed: POST https://token-issuer.internal/v1/sign 403
```

kevin: that 403 on /sign is classic SA-token creator missing. which SA is the runner using?

marta: ci-dast@staging-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com (we recently moved a bunch of SAs into a single infra group).

devops-bot: NOTE: RBAC change CR-2026-05-01 applied by infra-ops at 2026-05-01T18:22:00Z, removed "group:old-scanner-admins" binding from multiple service accounts.

kevin: confirm: token-issuer requires serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target SA and the runner SA must have roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on the service that creates ephemeral creds. Also token-issuer itself needs cloudkms.decrypt when it unwraps CI secrets. can someone check KMS audit for decrypts around the job time?

sre-oncall: pulling logs... hmm KMS key audit in logging project shows decrypts from token-issuer at 09:04:05, but nothing from ci-dast SA. that makes sense because signing failed before KMS call. but Marta said earlier they couldn't find audit entries for the deployer SA in a related incident — is there a chance our sinks filter out service_account principals?

marta: when we triaged yesterday's RBAC tidy we noticed the logging sink filter had a term excluding "serviceAccount:infra-*" for noise reduction. maybe too broad.

security-bot: ACTION: created ticket SEC-2475 "DAST runner token-issuer binding + KMS audit filter" and added label incident-minor.

kevin: mitigation idea: temporary patch is to re-grant iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to ci-dast@ for 30m and re-run the workflow. command: 
```
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding ci-dast@staging-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member=serviceAccount:token-issuer@infra-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
```

marta: I can request infra-admin to apply ephemeral grant, but can we also check the KMS sink filter at the same time so we don't miss audit evidence?

sre-oncall: yes will check sink. if the sink excludes infra SAs we should update sink filter to keep key admin/audit logs. quick check command: 
- gcloud logging sinks describe projects/logging-project/sinks/key-audit-sink

kevin: after ephemeral grant, confirm signed-cred POST succeeds and scan reaches the target. also verify KMS decrypt entries for token-issuer show up. if audit entries still missing, check that audit logs are enabled for the KMS key (cloudkms.googleapis.com).

marta: infra-admin applied ephemeral grant at 09:18, re-run started. update: the scan started, but we still saw 6 DAST alerts — looks like previous suppressions for generated test harness code weren't applied. runner fetched suppression file from internal config just fine though.

marta: final run logs: 
```
2026-05-02T09:19:22Z token-issuer: signed credential issued for ci-dast@ at 09:19:20
2026-05-02T09:19:23Z dast-runner: fetched suppressions from https://internal-config.company/dast/suppressions.json
2026-05-02T09:19:25Z dast-runner: scan complete: alerts total=6 (expected generation-related=4, new=2)
2026-05-02T09:19:25Z logging: KMS decrypt entry: principalPayload=serviceAccount:token-issuer@infra-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

kevin: good. next steps: 1) re-add the minimal tokenCreator binding permanently but scoped to the specific token-issuer principal and limited resource; 2) widen logging sink to include cloudkms audit entries from token-issuer and related infra SAs; 3) add preflight step in GH workflow to check token mint and suppression fetch before expensive scan step; 4) move generated-test suppressions into the repo or incorporate a trusted object store signed-URL flow so suppression fetch doesn't rely on single-SA ACL.

sre-oncall: I'll open INFRA-2201 to update sink filter and INFRA-2202 for permanent binding with least-privilege notes.

marta: I'll open SEC-2476 to add GH preflight and a repo suppression file PR. tagging reviewers.

kevin: small postmortem note: avoid broad log exclusions for serviceAccount principals; they hide useful audit evidence during RBAC churn.

marta: thanks all :white_check_mark: — closing once PRs and infra tickets are linked to SEC-2475.
